report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Rigorous clinical trials demonstrate that adding pharmaceutical-grade oral cannabidiol (CBD) to standard antiepileptic medications significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children and young adults with drug-resistant Dravet syndrome.

### Key Evidence
* **Landmark Randomized Controlled Trial:** A double-blind study published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated 120 children and young adults with Dravet syndrome. Patients receiving add-on cannabidiol (20 mg/kg/day) experienced a reduction in median monthly convulsive seizures from 12.4 to 5.9, compared to a minimal change from 14.9 to 14.1 in the placebo group. Overall, 43% of CBD-treated patients achieved a $\ge 50\%$ reduction in convulsive seizure frequency.
* **Dose-Ranging Trial:** A 2020 randomized clinical trial published in *JAMA Neurology* involving 199 patients confirmed that both 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day adjunctive CBD doses significantly decreased convulsive seizure frequency (48.7% and 45.7% reductions, respectively) compared with placebo (26.9%).
* **Regulatory Approval:** On the basis of these pivotal trials, the U.S. FDA approved Epidiolex (a purified cannabidiol oral solution) as an adjunctive therapy for treating seizures associated with Dravet syndrome.

### Sources
* *New England Journal of Medicine* Trial: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618
* *JAMA Neurology* Trial: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration Approval Announcement: https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-comprised-active-ingredient-derived-marijuana-treat-rare-severe-forms
